posts.text:
🇺🇸🇮🇷 What if Washington blames Iran for the FAA blackout? There’s no hotline to Tehran to stop a war by mistake

Robert Pape puts the odds that Iran was behind Friday’s outage at only 3 or 4 out of 10, and that number still scares him.

The University of Chicago professor says the danger is what each side does while nobody knows, because the US, Iran and Israel are all braced for the other to swing first.

If US intelligence ever got 75% sure it was Tehran, he argues any president would struggle to walk away, and nothing like the old red phone to Moscow exists to clear up a scare.

Robert on how standoffs like this usually go:

“It does not end well. And it’s because people have the itchy trigger fingers.”

Officials still call it a telecom outage, so everything now rides on who gets blamed.

Would you bet a war on a 75% guess? Starting one over a hunch would be the worst way for this fight to restart.

@ProfessorPape
